# windows_file (Data Source)

Reads the observed metadata of an existing file on a remote Windows host without managing it.

Metadata only by design: the data source exposes the file digest (`content_sha256`), size and last write time, never the file content itself, so host secrets are not persisted into Terraform state. Use the digest for existence checks, `triggers` blocks and pre-deploy reads.

Declarative attributes of the sibling resource (`content`, `source`, `source_url`, `encoding`, `overwrite`, `create_parent_directories`, `attributes`) are intentionally absent: the observed metadata is exposed read-only instead.

Returns an error when the file does not exist on the target host.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Look up the observed metadata of an existing file (metadata only: no content).
data "windows_file" "app_conf" {
  path = "C:\\data\\app.conf"
}

output "app_conf_sha256" {
  value = data.windows_file.app_conf.content_sha256
}

output "app_conf_size_bytes" {
  value = data.windows_file.app_conf.size_bytes
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `path` (String) Absolute path of the file on the target host. The file must already exist.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `content_sha256` (String) SHA-256 digest of the file content in lowercase hex, as observed on the host.
- `id` (String) Data source identifier: the normalised absolute path of the file.
- `last_write_time` (String) Last write timestamp of the file, ISO 8601 UTC, as observed on the host.
- `size_bytes` (Number) Size of the file in bytes, as observed on the host.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
